name: ONE-EYED JACK
description: One-Eyed Jack is a card-and-board game played in the Eastern USA. A 10x10 board has spaces corresponding to playing cards. Players use cards from hand to place chips on matching board spaces; the goal is to form rows of five chips. Two-eyed jacks (clubs, diamonds) are wildâ€”place a chip on any empty space. content.text: One-Eyed Jack is a card-and-board game played in the Eastern USA. A 10x10 board has spaces corresponding to playing cards. Players use cards from hand to place chips on matching board spaces; the goal is to form rows of five chips. Two-eyed jacks (clubs, diamonds) are wildâ€”place a chip on any empty space. One-eyed jacks (hearts, spades) remove an opponent's chip from the board.
Played in parts of the Eastern USA (North Carolina, Tennessee). Often home-made with a second deck cut and glued to form the board. Jax published a commercial version in 1982 under the name Sequence.
2, 3, or 4 players. Four typically play as partners (opposite seats).
Two standard 52-card packs (104 cards). Board: 50 card-spaces from a second deck (4 jacks removed; 2 jokers = corner spaces).
Two decks, board (10x10 with card faces in cells; jokers in corners), chips: 50 per colour (2 players/teams) or 40 per colour (3 players).
1. Deal 7 (2 players), 6 (3 players), or 5 (4 players) cards to each player. 2. Remaining cards form the stock.

items.text: Draw at Start: Draw a card at the start of your turn instead of the end.
One-Eyed Jack Places: One-eyed jack can place a chip on any space (even occupied), replacing the token there.
One-Eyed Cannot Break Row: One-eyed jack cannot remove a chip from a completed five-chip row.
Dead Card Draw: If both spaces for a card are occupied, holder may discard it and draw a replacement (does not count as a turn).
